# FM-1 projects

> Drew Robinson's open-source projects for the M-VAVE FM-1, a tiny hardware synthesiser: ESTAMPIE (custom firmware), FM-SWITCH (an iPhone, iPad and Mac app for swapping firmwares) and FM1Kit (the Swift package for installing firmware that the app is built on). None of them is affiliated with M-VAVE.

All three are on GitHub under github.com/ocean. Installing custom firmware on an FM-1 is at the owner's own risk. This site itself is under CC BY 4.0: reuse it with credit to Drew Robinson.

## Projects

- [ESTAMPIE](https://fm-1.drewr.dev/estampie/): a mediæval groovebox firmware for the FM-1, forked from GHOULBOX and Felucca (GPL-3.0). Source: https://github.com/ocean/estampie
- [FM-SWITCH](https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm-switch/): a SwiftUI app for iOS, iPadOS and macOS that installs FM-1 firmwares over USB. iPhone and iPad in TestFlight; the Mac app is a signed, notarised download. Source: https://github.com/ocean/FM-SWITCH
- [FM1Kit](https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm1kit/): a Swift package (MIT) that speaks the FM-1's firmware update protocol over USB-MIDI, installs m-bootloader, and on a Mac backs up, restores and writes the whole flash in the chip's USB download mode. Source: https://github.com/ocean/FM1Kit

## For firmware developers

- [Bootloader check](https://fm-1.drewr.dev/bootloader-check/): FM-1 firmwares built on Felucca's original update code refuse V15 and V16 once the FM-1's bootloader has changed (by M-VAVE's V16, m-bootloader, or Open V12 or V14), and usually every other firmware not built on Felucca, so their users can only install Felucca-based firmwares over USB. V16 and m-bootloader work correctly; the cause is a safety check in the firmwares' update code. Many firmwares also only know the older flash chip (P25Q80), so on FM-1s sold since autumn 2026 (UC25HQ80, JEDEC ID 0xB36014) they keep saves only until the FM-1 is switched off. The page lists which firmwares, what each is built on (fm1-base, felucca-bsp or its own copy of Felucca's) and which chips each release knows, with the fixes: port felucca-bsp afd83ede, and accept 0xB36014 as Felucca's f4cbb6a2 does. Data: https://fm-1.drewr.dev/bootloader-check/data.json

## Research

- [The FM-1 Moment](https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm1-moment/): a dated, sourced history of the FM-1's custom-firmware boom in 2026 (the device, the first custom firmware on 27 September, Felucca and the first open-source wave from 3 October, the community's tools, M-VAVE's own open firmware from 16 October, and about 200 firmwares by 31 October). Data: https://fm-1.drewr.dev/fm1-moment/releases.csv
